item.title: US Strikes Iranian Tankers After Attack on US Warships
item.description: Bloomberg This Weekend has breaking news that US forces struck three Iranian crude carriers after the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles toward two US Navy warships, according to US Central Command. The renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz adds pressure to shipping and energy markets as President Donald Trump continues to downplay the conflict as something short of war. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Esper Raises Concern Over Pentagon Leadership Loss
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper calls the Pentagon’s polygraph testing of roughly 50 Joint Staff members unprecedented in scale as officials investigate leaks about US munitions stocks. Esper tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that he is less concerned about immediate combat readiness than the institutional impact of leadership turnover and its potential effect on the military’s tradition of an apolitical officer corps. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EU Envoy Urges Maximum Pressure on Russia
item.description: EU Ambassador to the United States Jovita Neliupšienė joins Bloomberg This Weekend and discusses with hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that Europe must keep supporting Ukraine while applying “maximum pressure” on Moscow because Russia has not changed its war aims. The comments come as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner visit Moscow before heading to Kyiv in an effort to revive stalled peace negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You Should See
item.description: Canned cocktails, the science behind the Gen Z stare and the US Open becoming a food fest: Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason to hear about the headlines from this week you may have missed but need to check out. Watch, on Bloomberg This Weekend! Live Saturday and Sunday, 7am - 10am EST on Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI May Transform How Humans Understand Animals
item.description: Researchers are using AI to analyze vast collections of animal vocalizations, looking for patterns that could help humans better understand how species such as crows communicate. Bloomberg Weekend Senior Writer Morgan Meaker is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says the technology could reshape humans’ relationship with animals, but researchers warn it also raises ethical questions about privacy, exploitation and how those discoveries might be used. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Singapore Government Won’t Interfere in Decisions on Air India
item.description: The Singapore government said it will not interfere in any decision that Singapore Airlines Ltd. makes in Air India Ltd., which is said to be seeking financial aid from its shareholders.
item.dc:creator: Shamim Adam

item.title: Energy Markets Strained by Iran, Ukraine Wars
item.description: Renewed US-Iran fighting and uncertainty over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz are adding pressure to global energy markets, while the threat of mines continues to deter some traffic. Ukraine’s attacks on Russian refineries are compounding tight diesel supplies, creating what Bloomberg News Oil Products Reporter Will Kubzansky describes as a distillates crisis heading into peak demand season. Also joining Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss the situation is Bloomberg News Middle East Correspondent Abeer Abu Omar. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Women Are Shaping Drag Racing
item.description: Drag racing has outpaced Formula 1, NASCAR and IndyCar on inclusivity, offering a model for sports that still treat women competing at the highest level as a novelty, Bloomberg Opinion columnist Adam Minter says. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Leonardo CEO Mariani Sees Ukraine Unit as Acquisition Outpost
item.description: Leonardo SpA, the Italian state-controlled defense company, is aiming to deepen ties with Ukraine’s fast-growing military-technology sector through its new Kyiv unit, seeking partnership, investment or acquisition opportunities, Chief Executive Officer Lorenzo Mariani said.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Brambilla

item.title: Philippines’ VP Duterte Posts Bail, Says She Fears for Her Life
item.description: Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail for a criminal case accusing her of threatening to kill President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. She said she fears for her own life.
item.dc:creator: Cliff Venzon

item.title: Europe’s Wealth Managers Are Turning Their Backs on Stock Rally
item.description: More European wealth managers have turned pessimistic on the region’s stocks, taking the view that this year’s rally is likely to falter while markets in the US and developing countries power ahead.
item.dc:creator: Margaryta Kirakosian and Levin Stamm

item.title: Malaysia’s PAS Party Wants Nationwide Gambling License Review
item.description: Parti Islam Se-Malaysia, which leads the country’s main opposition bloc, said the government should review existing gambling licenses and stop giving new ones, its latest effort to curb social ills.
item.dc:creator: Kok Leong Chan

item.title: HK’s Lee Says City to Expand Offshore Yuan Usage in 5-Year Plan
item.description: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee said the city’s first five-year plan will focus on areas including expanding offshore yuan usage and cross-border investment with the mainland.
item.dc:creator: Echo Wong

item.title: Bloom Energy, Illumina, Everpure to Join S&P 500 This Month
item.description: Bloom Energy Corp., Illumina Inc. and Everpure Inc. will join the S&P 500 in the latest quarterly rebalance, S&P Dow Jones Indices said Friday.
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Lee

item.title: Acuerdo de Trump con Venezuela inquieta a petroleras de EE.UU.
item.description: El presidente Donald Trump se ha jactado de que su amplio acuerdo petrolero con Venezuela, que en la práctica da a Estados Unidos control sobre gran parte de la riqueza petrolera del país, es posiblemente “el mejor acuerdo jamás firmado”.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Kevin Crowley and David Wethe

item.title: S&P Downgrades Senegal After Government Unveils Debt Rework
item.description: S&P Global Ratings cut Senegal’s credit score further into junk territory, saying a distressed debt exchange or default on the country’s foreign-currency commercial debt is “extremely likely” after the government launched a plan to restructure its obligations.
item.dc:creator: Vinícius Andrade

item.title: Hedge Funds Hike Bullish Oil Bets to May High as Iran War Flares
item.description: Hedge funds turned the most bullish on Brent crude since May as a fresh spate of fighting between the US and Iran heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis and Will Kubzansky

item.title: Wall Street Risk Complex Defies Rate Threat After Jobs Data
item.description: The global bond selloff is proving no wrecking ball for Wall Street, repricing the cost of money without setting off the usual scramble out of risk assets.
item.dc:creator: Isabelle Lee and Denitsa Tsekova

item.title: S&P 500 Ends Week Flat as Strong Jobs Growth Fuels Fed-Hike Bets
item.description: US stocks finished lower on Friday as the American economy added more jobs than expected in August, raising expectations that the Federal Reserve may hike interest rates soon.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: Emerging Currencies Cap Longest Winning Streak Since 2007
item.description: An index for emerging-market currencies rose for a 10th successive week, its longest winning streak since 2007, even as a blowout US jobs report briefly jolted global markets on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Giovanna Bellotti Azevedo and Beatriz Amat
